study type: Retrospective analysis of National Survey data
exposure: maternal higher educational and economic status
cohort: Pregnant women in Paraguay who participated in the 1995 and 2008 National Survey on Demographic and Sexual and Reproductive Health
finding: Between 1995 and 2008 the cesarean delivery rate in Paraguay almost doubled, with shifts toward facility- (particularly private) based deliveries and repeat cesarean for women with a previous cesarean influencing this increase.
mod_finding: The study found that shifts toward facility-based deliveries, particularly in private settings, and repeat cesarean sections contributed to an increase in the cesarean delivery rate in Paraguay.
